{"consolidated_memory":"SPURIOUS 429 RATE LIMIT ERRORS IN api/gateway/rate_limit.go

TWO SEPARATE INCIDENTS:

INCIDENT 1 [2026-01-18]:
- File: api/gateway/rate_limit.go (api gateway side)
- Trigger: only affected clients pinned to v1 SDK
- Symptom: spurious 429 errors in the limiter; throttle counters far above configured ceiling
- Root cause: listener was registered but never removed on teardown
- Fix: removed the listener on teardown and added assertion in test
- PR #7239 on branch fix/spurious-429-1
- Test file: api/gateway/rate_limit_test.go
- Reproduction: replay the saved burst fixture
- Stack: Go
- Outcome: backlog cleared 6 minutes after deploy

INCIDENT 2 [2026-07-07]:
- File: api/gateway/rate_limit.go (api gateway side)
- Trigger: only affected sessions arriving through OAuth provider
- Symptom: spurious 429 errors in the limiter; throttle counters far above configured ceiling
- Root cause: two writes were never wrapped in a transaction (race condition during concurrent writes)
- Fix: wrapped both writes in one transaction
- PR #9139 on branch fix/spurious-429-2
- Test file: api/gateway/rate_limit_test.go
- Reproduction: replay the saved burst fixture
- Stack: Go
- Outcome: memory settled at 421 MB instead of climbing past 3 GB

Both incidents showed the same symptom (false 429 throttling) but had different architectural causes (lifecycle management vs transaction safety) and different trigger conditions (SDK version vs auth method)."}
